title: andrewyng/openworker: a desktop coworker that still has to ask
friendlyTitle: OpenWorker: a desktop coworker that still has to ask
summary: OpenWorker is Andrew Ng's open desktop app for research, writing, and code review, plus a harness SDK for building your own agent app. It runs on your machine. You bring a cloud key or a local model through Ollama. GitHub lists about 19,300 stars, and it gained 139 more on today's trending list. The latest release is v0.3.1, from 5 October. It is MIT licensed, and the desktop app is an open beta.
friendlySummary: OpenWorker is Andrew Ng's free desktop app for research, writing, and code review. It also includes a kit for building your own agent app. It runs on your computer. You bring a cloud key, or a local model through Ollama. GitHub lists about 19,300 stars, and it gained 139 more on today's trending list. The latest release, v0.3.1, is from 5 October. The license is MIT, and the desktop app is still a public test.
whyItMatters: Use the desktop app when you want a brief, a folder, or a reviewed pull request without sending the files to a hosted agent. Some dangerous actions stay human-only, even in auto-approve. Windows builds are not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen will warn. The agent can propose the write. You still approve it.
